terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; the cause in the ablative, or in + ablative
evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.27.66: gaudiō; Cic. Clu. 5.14: laetitiā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Rosc. Am. 6.16: victōriā; Cic. Balb. 26.58: in ruīnīs alicujus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The cause of joy goes in the ablative (exsultāre victōriā); gloating over another’s fall is in ruīnīs alicujus (Cic. Balb. 26.58, Lewis & Short).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 321.
